title: Allowance-aware tiered router for free / paid / enterprise plans
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement an allowance-aware routing layer that assigns incoming requests to plan-specific lanes (free, paid, enterprise) while respecting per-plan and per-tenant allowance signals. The router must: 1) prefer lowest-cost compatible model variant while meeting latency SLOs; 2) enforce soft and hard admission controls based on allowance balance (aka credits) with graceful degradation policies; 3) preserve regional affinity for data residency/latency; 4) integrate with existing fallback model variants and warm-pool reserves for enterprise customers. This ticket covers design, prototype, tests, and a canary rollout path.
acceptance_criteria: Router honors per-tenant allowance (credits) and exposes admit/deny/soft-degrade decisions in traces
Requests for enterprise plans never route to >best-effort model variant unless explicitly overloaded and warned
Free-tier requests are subject to adaptive polite-throttling rather than immediate hard-deny and can be soft-demoted to smaller quantized variants
Regional selection respects customer region preference when capacity is available; fallback chooses nearest compatible region
End-to-end throughput & p99 latency regressions <= 5% relative to baseline for canary traffic (measured on staging)
decisions: Use an 'allowance' signal (rolling token budget per tenant) instead of raw quota counters to smooth spikes — EWMA window of 5 minutes for consumption smoothing

Admission controller will expose three outcomes: admit (full-quality), degrade (route to quantized/smaller model), hold (enqueue for short window) or reject (hard deny). Hold will be used only for <500ms windows to preserve latency SLOs
Model mapping: each plan maps to an ordered list of compatible model variants. Router tries highest-ranked variant where allowance and capacity permit, otherwise falls back in order
Regional policy: prefer same-region serving when capacity ratio > 0.8, otherwise allow cross-region fallback with region-penalty scoring
Enterprise warm-pools: reserve a small fraction of capacity (configurable per account) that bypasses degradation under normal conditions; paid accounts use soft-reserve
Telemetry: emit 'routing.decision' event with fields: plan, tenant_id, allowance_before, allowance_after, chosen_variant, chosen_region, decision_reason

Canary rollout: 5% internal -> 25% beta orgs -> full rollout if metrics are green

2026-02-20 Lena Chen (Review): Concerned about additional per-request latency from allowance-check RPC. Proposal: co-locate allowance cache in routing node with 10s TTL and async refresh. If cache miss, fall back to fast read path.
2026-02-24 Diego Marquez: Implemented local allowance cache and added fast-path that treats small allowance divergences as acceptable for soft-degrades. See PR #612.

2026-02-28 Owen Park (SRE): Load test scenario B exposed p99 spike at 90th percentile traffic due to region-churn when cross-region fallback bursts. Mitigation: add cooldown per-tenant region failover of 30s.

2026-03-08 Diego Marquez: Telemetry events added to staging traces. Verified routing.decision fields appear in Jaeger and are linked to Datadog metrics. Draft dashboard link above.
